section_1.title: The Cheetah's Journey: Speed vs. Distance
section_1.content: Introduce the big picture through a real-world scenario. Explain that motion can be viewed in two ways: how fast you are going at an instant (Derivative) and how much ground you've covered in total (Integral).
section_1.example: An animation of a Cheetah running. A 'Speedometer' shows its instantaneous velocity (Derivative), while an 'Odometer' tracks its total displacement (Integral). The goal is to show that if you know one, you can find the other.

section_2.title: Prerequisite Recap: Slope and Area
section_2.content: Briefly revisit the graphical meaning of both concepts to build a foundation. Define the Derivative as the 'Slope' of a tangent line and the Definite Integral as the 'Area' under a curve.
section_2.example: A split-screen visual: On the left, a line touching a curve at one point (Slope/Rate). On the right, the region under a curve filled with color (Area/Accumulation).

section_3.title: The Accumulation Function
section_3.content: Introduce a 'growing' area. If we have a function f(t), let's define a new function A(x) that calculates the area from a fixed start point to a moving point 'x'. This is the 'Area Function'.
section_3.example: A graph of a curve where a vertical 'curtain' moves from left to right. As the curtain moves, the shaded area increases. This changing area is represented by a new growing graph below it.

section_4.title: The Core Insight: How Fast Does Area Grow?
section_4.content: Ask the critical question: At what rate is the shaded area increasing at any moment 'x'? Demonstrate visually that the 'extra slice' of area added is proportional to the height of the original function f(x).
section_4.example: Zoom into the edge of the moving 'curtain' from Section 3. Show a tiny sliver of width 'dx'. The area added is approximately f(x) times dx. Therefore, the rate of change of Area (dA/dx) is exactly the height of the curve f(x).

section_5.title: The Fundamental Theorem: Two Sides of a Coin
section_5.content: Synthesize the observation: Differentiation and Integration are inverse operations. If you integrate a function to get the area, and then differentiate that area, you get the original function back.
section_5.example: A 'Mathematical Loop' animation: Start with f(x) -> Integrate -> Get Area Function F(x) -> Differentiate -> Return to f(x). Use the analogy of a 'climbing' robot (Integration) and its 'downhill' speed sensor (Differentiation).

section_6.title: Application: The Power of the Relationship
section_6.content: Explain why this matters: We can find areas without drawing thousands of tiny rectangles. We just need to find the 'Anti-derivative'.
section_6.example: Calculating the area under a parabola y=x². Instead of counting blocks, we find its anti-derivative (x³/3), plug in the endpoints, and get the exact area instantly. The Cheetah's total distance is simply the 'anti-derivative' of its speed function.

section_1.title: The Cheetah's Journey: Speed vs. Distance
section_1.content: Introduce the big picture through a real-world scenario. Explain that motion can be viewed in two ways: how fast you are going at an instant (Derivative) and how much ground you've covered in total (Integral).
section_1.example: An animation of a Cheetah running. A 'Speedometer' shows its instantaneous velocity (Derivative), while an 'Odometer' tracks its total displacement (Integral). The goal is to show that if you know one, you can find the other.

section_2.title: Prerequisite Recap: Slope and Area
section_2.content: Briefly revisit the graphical meaning of both concepts to build a foundation. Define the Derivative as the 'Slope' of a tangent line and the Definite Integral as the 'Area' under a curve.
section_2.example: A split-screen visual: On the left, a line touching a curve at one point (Slope/Rate). On the right, the region under a curve filled with color (Area/Accumulation).

section_3.title: The Accumulation Function
section_3.content: Introduce a 'growing' area. If we have a function f(t), let's define a new function A(x) that calculates the area from a fixed start point to a moving point 'x'. This is the 'Area Function'.
section_3.example: A graph of a curve where a vertical 'curtain' moves from left to right. As the curtain moves, the shaded area increases. This changing area is represented by a new growing graph below it.

section_4.title: The Core Insight: How Fast Does Area Grow?
section_4.content: Ask the critical question: At what rate is the shaded area increasing at any moment 'x'? Demonstrate visually that the 'extra slice' of area added is proportional to the height of the original function f(x).
section_4.example: Zoom into the edge of the moving 'curtain' from Section 3. Show a tiny sliver of width 'dx'. The area added is approximately f(x) times dx. Therefore, the rate of change of Area (dA/dx) is exactly the height of the curve f(x).

section_5.title: The Fundamental Theorem: Two Sides of a Coin
section_5.content: Synthesize the observation: Differentiation and Integration are inverse operations. If you integrate a function to get the area, and then differentiate that area, you get the original function back.
section_5.example: A 'Mathematical Loop' animation: Start with f(x) -> Integrate -> Get Area Function F(x) -> Differentiate -> Return to f(x). Use the analogy of a 'climbing' robot (Integration) and its 'downhill' speed sensor (Differentiation).

section_6.title: Application: The Power of the Relationship
section_6.content: Explain why this matters: We can find areas without drawing thousands of tiny rectangles. We just need to find the 'Anti-derivative'.
section_6.example: Calculating the area under a parabola y=x². Instead of counting blocks, we find its anti-derivative (x³/3), plug in the endpoints, and get the exact area instantly. The Cheetah's total distance is simply the 'anti-derivative' of its speed function.

section_1.title: The Cheetah's Journey: Speed vs. Distance
lecture_lines: Meet our cheetah racing across the savanna.
Speedometer shows its instantaneous speed, the derivative.
Odometer tracks total distance covered, the integral.
animations: Fade in a Cheetah silhouette (#D4AF37) moving across the screen.
Display a circular Speedometer (#FFFFFF) with a needle fluctuating.
Show an Odometer (#FFFFFF) with digits increasing as Cheetah moves.
Highlight the Speedometer; label it "Derivative of Distance" (#00FFFF).
Highlight the Odometer; label it "Integral of Speed" (#FFD700).

section_2.title: Prerequisite Recap: Slope and Area
lecture_lines: Recall that derivatives represent the slope of curves.
In contrast, integrals represent the area under curves.
We will now link these two fundamental concepts.
animations: Draw a green curve (#00FF00); animate a magenta tangent line (#FF00FF) sliding along it.
Shade the area under a different part of the green curve (#00FF00) in light green.
Display labels "Slope (Rate)" and "Area (Accumulation)" in white (#FFFFFF) on opposite sides.

section_3.title: The Accumulation Function
lecture_lines: Imagine a moving curtain sweeping across a graph.
Shaded area grows as the curtain moves right.
This growing area defines the accumulation function.
As input x increases, the total area accumulates.
This function maps points to their total area.
animations: Draw a green curve f(t) (#00FF00); show a vertical white line (#FFFFFF) at t=0.
Move the vertical line to the right to x; shade the area A(x) (#00FF00) as it moves.
Simultaneously plot a new orange curve A(x) (#FF8C00) below, representing the total area.

section_4.title: The Core Insight: How Fast Does Area Grow?
lecture_lines: How fast does this accumulated area actually grow?
Consider a tiny sliver added at position x.
The sliver height is exactly the function's height.
Area added equals height times the tiny width.
The growth rate is the original function's height.
animations: Zoom into the edge of the shaded area at x; show a thin rectangle (#FFFF00) of width dx.
Label the height of the rectangle f(x) (#00FF00) and the width dx (#FFFFFF).
Show the formula dA = f(x) * dx in yellow (#FFFF00).
Rearrange the formula to dA/dx = f(x) with a transform animation.
Highlight the result: the slope of A(x) is f(x).

section_5.title: The Fundamental Theorem: Two Sides of a Coin
lecture_lines: The area's derivative is the original function's height.
Differentiation and integration are inverse operations.
Integrating a rate gives you the total accumulation.
Differentiating accumulation returns the original rate.
They are two sides of the same coin.
animations: Place f(x) (#00FF00) at the top; draw a clockwise arrow labeled "Integrate" (#00FFFF).
The arrow leads to F(x) (#FF8C00) at the bottom.
Draw another clockwise arrow labeled "Differentiate" (#FF00FF) from F(x) back to f(x).
Flash the entire loop in white (#FFFFFF) to emphasize the cycle.
Display the text "Fundamental Theorem of Calculus" (#FFFFFF) in the center of the loop.

section_6.title: Application: The Power of the Relationship
lecture_lines: This relationship lets us calculate areas with ease.
Find the anti-derivative to solve complex integrals.
Total distance is simply the anti-derivative of speed.
animations: Plot y=x^2 (#00FF00); shade the area from x=0 to x=2.
Display the anti-derivative F(x) = x^3/3 (#FFFFFF) next to the graph.
Calculate F(2) - F(0) = 8/3; update the area label to "8/3" (#FFFF00).

outline.title: The Accumulation Function
outline.content: Introduce a 'growing' area. If we have a function f(t), let's define a new function A(x) that calculates the area from a fixed start point to a moving point 'x'. This is the 'Area Function'.
outline.example: A graph of a curve where a vertical 'curtain' moves from left to right. As the curtain moves, the shaded area increases. This changing area is represented by a new growing graph below it.

storyboard.title: The Accumulation Function
lecture_lines: Imagine a moving curtain sweeping across a graph.
Shaded area grows as the curtain moves right.
This growing area defines the accumulation function.
As input x increases, the total area accumulates.
This function maps points to their total area.
animations: Draw a green curve f(t) (#00FF00); show a vertical white line (#FFFFFF) at t=0.
Move the vertical line to the right to x; shade the area A(x) (#00FF00) as it moves.
Simultaneously plot a new orange curve A(x) (#FF8C00) below, representing the total area.

outline.title: Prerequisite Recap: Slope and Area
outline.content: Briefly revisit the graphical meaning of both concepts to build a foundation. Define the Derivative as the 'Slope' of a tangent line and the Definite Integral as the 'Area' under a curve.
outline.example: A split-screen visual: On the left, a line touching a curve at one point (Slope/Rate). On the right, the region under a curve filled with color (Area/Accumulation).

storyboard.title: Prerequisite Recap: Slope and Area
lecture_lines: Recall that derivatives represent the slope of curves.
In contrast, integrals represent the area under curves.
We will now link these two fundamental concepts.
animations: Draw a green curve (#00FF00); animate a magenta tangent line (#FF00FF) sliding along it.
Shade the area under a different part of the green curve (#00FF00) in light green.
Display labels "Slope (Rate)" and "Area (Accumulation)" in white (#FFFFFF) on opposite sides.

outline.title: Application: The Power of the Relationship
outline.content: Explain why this matters: We can find areas without drawing thousands of tiny rectangles. We just need to find the 'Anti-derivative'.
outline.example: Calculating the area under a parabola y=x². Instead of counting blocks, we find its anti-derivative (x³/3), plug in the endpoints, and get the exact area instantly. The Cheetah's total distance is simply the 'anti-derivative' of its speed function.

storyboard.title: Application: The Power of the Relationship
lecture_lines: This relationship lets us calculate areas with ease.
Find the anti-derivative to solve complex integrals.
Total distance is simply the anti-derivative of speed.
animations: Plot y=x^2 (#00FF00); shade the area from x=0 to x=2.
Display the anti-derivative F(x) = x^3/3 (#FFFFFF) next to the graph.
Calculate F(2) - F(0) = 8/3; update the area label to "8/3" (#FFFF00).

outline.title: The Fundamental Theorem: Two Sides of a Coin
outline.content: Synthesize the observation: Differentiation and Integration are inverse operations. If you integrate a function to get the area, and then differentiate that area, you get the original function back.
outline.example: A 'Mathematical Loop' animation: Start with f(x) -> Integrate -> Get Area Function F(x) -> Differentiate -> Return to f(x). Use the analogy of a 'climbing' robot (Integration) and its 'downhill' speed sensor (Differentiation).

storyboard.title: The Fundamental Theorem: Two Sides of a Coin
lecture_lines: The area's derivative is the original function's height.
Differentiation and integration are inverse operations.
Integrating a rate gives you the total accumulation.
Differentiating accumulation returns the original rate.
They are two sides of the same coin.
animations: Place f(x) (#00FF00) at the top; draw a clockwise arrow labeled "Integrate" (#00FFFF).
The arrow leads to F(x) (#FF8C00) at the bottom.
Draw another clockwise arrow labeled "Differentiate" (#FF00FF) from F(x) back to f(x).
Flash the entire loop in white (#FFFFFF) to emphasize the cycle.
Display the text "Fundamental Theorem of Calculus" (#FFFFFF) in the center of the loop.

outline.title: The Core Insight: How Fast Does Area Grow?
outline.content: Ask the critical question: At what rate is the shaded area increasing at any moment 'x'? Demonstrate visually that the 'extra slice' of area added is proportional to the height of the original function f(x).
outline.example: Zoom into the edge of the moving 'curtain' from Section 3. Show a tiny sliver of width 'dx'. The area added is approximately f(x) times dx. Therefore, the rate of change of Area (dA/dx) is exactly the height of the curve f(x).

storyboard.title: The Core Insight: How Fast Does Area Grow?
lecture_lines: How fast does this accumulated area actually grow?
Consider a tiny sliver added at position x.
The sliver height is exactly the function's height.
Area added equals height times the tiny width.
The growth rate is the original function's height.
animations: Zoom into the edge of the shaded area at x; show a thin rectangle (#FFFF00) of width dx.
Label the height of the rectangle f(x) (#00FF00) and the width dx (#FFFFFF).
Show the formula dA = f(x) * dx in yellow (#FFFF00).
Rearrange the formula to dA/dx = f(x) with a transform animation.
Highlight the result: the slope of A(x) is f(x).

                y = 2.2 - i * 1

        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):

                m.set_points_as_corners([bottom_axes.c2p(t, A_func(t)) for t in t_vals])
        a_trace.add_updater(update_trace)

        )

        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.play(

        # Data from storyboard

        lecture_lines = [
            "Meet our cheetah racing across the savanna.",

            "Odometer tracks total distance covered, the integral."

        # Update lecture colors
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(INTEGRAL_COLOR)
        
        # Odometer: Box with increasing digits
        odometer_box = Rectangle(width=1.2, height=0.4, color=ODOMETER_COLOR)
        self.place_at_grid(odometer_box, "F2")

        self.place_at_grid(odo_label, "F3")
        
        self.play(Create(odometer_box), Write(distance_val), Write(odo_label))
        self.play(time_tracker.animate.set_value(6), run_time=3, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(1)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Data from storyboard
        title = "Prerequisite Recap: Slope and Area"
        lecture_lines = [
            "- Recall that derivatives represent the slope of curves.",
            "- In contrast, integrals represent the area under curves.",
            "- We will now link these two fundamental concepts."
        ]
        
        # Initialize layout
        self.setup_layout(title, lecture_lines)
        
        # Colors from storyboard/issues
        GREEN_CURVE = "#00FF00"
        MAGENTA_SLOPE = "#FF00FF"
        LIGHT_GREEN_AREA = "#90EE90"
        WHITE_COLOR = "#FFFFFF"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Highlight lecture line 1 in Magenta (matching tangent/slope visual)
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(MAGENTA_SLOPE))

        # Setup Axes in the right-side grid area (A1 to F6)
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[-3, 3, 1],
            y_range=[-2, 2, 1],
            x_length=5,
            y_length=4,
            axis_config={"include_tip": True, "color": WHITE_COLOR}
        ).set_z_index(0)
        self.place_in_area(axes, "A1", "F6")
        
        # Parabolic curve: y = 0.2x^2 - 1
        curve = axes.plot(lambda x: 0.2 * x**2 - 1, color=GREEN_CURVE)
        
        # ValueTracker for the tangent point x-coordinate
        t_val = ValueTracker(-2)
        
        # Dot at the tangent point
        dot = Dot(color=MAGENTA_SLOPE).set_z_index(2)
        dot.add_updater(lambda m: m.move_to(axes.c2p(t_val.get_value(), 0.2 * t_val.get_value()**2 - 1)))
        
        # Tangent line updated dynamically
        tangent_line = Line(color=MAGENTA_SLOPE).set_z_index(1)
        def update_tangent(m):
            x = t_val.get_value()
            y = 0.2 * x**2 - 1
            slope = 0.4 * x
            # Determine start and end points for a fixed length tangent
            p1 = axes.c2p(x - 0.8, y - slope * 0.8)
            p2 = axes.c2p(x + 0.8, y + slope * 0.8)
            m.put_start_and_end_on(p1, p2)
        tangent_line.add_updater(update_tangent)

        self.play(Create(axes), Create(curve))
        self.add(dot, tangent_line)
        # Animate the tangent sliding along the curve
        self.play(t_val.animate.set_value(0.5), run_time=3, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Highlight lecture line 2 in Light Green (matching area visual)
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(LIGHT_GREEN_AREA))
        
        # Create and animate the shaded area under the curve
        # Area from x = 0.5 to x = 2.5
        shaded_area = axes.get_area(curve, x_range=[0.5, 2.5], color=LIGHT_GREEN_AREA, opacity=0.4)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(shaded_area))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Transition to linking the concepts
        # Line 3 stays white
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE_COLOR))
        
        # Create labels
        label_slope = Text("Slope (Rate)", font_size=24, color=WHITE_COLOR)
        label_area = Text("Area (Accumulation)", font_size=24, color=WHITE_COLOR)
        
        # Position labels using grid
        self.place_at_grid(label_slope, "B2")  # Top left quadrant
        self.place_at_grid(label_area, "E5")   # Bottom right quadrant
        
        self.play(
            Write(label_slope),
            Write(label_area)
        )
        self.wait(2)

        # Highlight lecture line 1 in Magenta (matching tangent/slope visual)
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(MAGENTA_SLOPE))

        # Setup Axes in the right-side grid area (A1 to F6)
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[-3, 3, 1],
            y_range=[-2, 2, 1],
            x_length=5,
            y_length=4,
            axis_config={"include_tip": True, "color": WHITE_COLOR}
        ).set_z_index(0)
        self.place_in_area(axes, "A1", "F6")
        
        # Parabolic curve: y = 0.2x^2 - 1
        curve = axes.plot(lambda x: 0.2 * x**2 - 1, color=GREEN_CURVE)
        
        # ValueTracker for the tangent point x-coordinate
        t_val = ValueTracker(-2)
        
        # Dot at the tangent point
        dot = Dot(color=MAGENTA_SLOPE).set_z_index(2)
        dot.add_updater(lambda m: m.move_to(axes.c2p(t_val.get_value(), 0.2 * t_val.get_value()**2 - 1)))
        
        # Tangent line updated dynamically
        tangent_line = Line(color=MAGENTA_SLOPE).set_z_index(1)
        def update_tangent(m):
            x = t_val.get_value()
            y = 0.2 * x**2 - 1
            slope = 0.4 * x
            # Determine start and end points for a fixed length tangent
            p1 = axes.c2p(x - 0.8, y - slope * 0.8)
            p2 = axes.c2p(x + 0.8, y + slope * 0.8)
            m.put_start_and_end_on(p1, p2)
        tangent_line.add_updater(update_tangent)

        self.play(Create(axes), Create(curve))
        self.add(dot, tangent_line)
        # Animate the tangent sliding along the curve
        self.play(t_val.animate.set_value(0.5), run_time=3, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Highlight lecture line 2 in Light Green (matching area visual)
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(LIGHT_GREEN_AREA))
        
        # Create and animate the shaded area under the curve
        # Area from x = 0.5 to x = 2.5
        shaded_area = axes.get_area(curve, x_range=[0.5, 2.5], color=LIGHT_GREEN_AREA, opacity=0.4)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(shaded_area))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Transition to linking the concepts
        # Line 3 stays white
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE_COLOR))
        
        # Create labels
        label_slope = Text("Slope (Rate)", font_size=24, color=WHITE_COLOR)
        label_area = Text("Area (Accumulation)", font_size=24, color=WHITE_COLOR)
        
        # Position labels using grid
        self.place_at_grid(label_slope, "B2")  # Top left quadrant
        self.place_at_grid(label_area, "E5")   # Bottom right quadrant
        
        self.play(
            Write(label_slope),
            Write(label_area)
        )
        self.wait(2)

section_1.title: The Cheetah's Journey: Speed vs. Distance
section_1.content: Introduce the big picture through a real-world scenario. Explain that motion can be viewed in two ways: how fast you are going at an instant (Derivative) and how much ground you've covered in total (Integral).
section_1.example: An animation of a Cheetah running. A 'Speedometer' shows its instantaneous velocity (Derivative), while an 'Odometer' tracks its total displacement (Integral). The goal is to show that if you know one, you can find the other.

section_2.title: Prerequisite Recap: Slope and Area
section_2.content: Briefly revisit the graphical meaning of both concepts to build a foundation. Define the Derivative as the 'Slope' of a tangent line and the Definite Integral as the 'Area' under a curve.
section_2.example: A split-screen visual: On the left, a line touching a curve at one point (Slope/Rate). On the right, the region under a curve filled with color (Area/Accumulation).

section_3.title: The Accumulation Function
section_3.content: Introduce a 'growing' area. If we have a function f(t), let's define a new function A(x) that calculates the area from a fixed start point to a moving point 'x'. This is the 'Area Function'.
section_3.example: A graph of a curve where a vertical 'curtain' moves from left to right. As the curtain moves, the shaded area increases. This changing area is represented by a new growing graph below it.

section_4.title: The Core Insight: How Fast Does Area Grow?
section_4.content: Ask the critical question: At what rate is the shaded area increasing at any moment 'x'? Demonstrate visually that the 'extra slice' of area added is proportional to the height of the original function f(x).
section_4.example: Zoom into the edge of the moving 'curtain' from Section 3. Show a tiny sliver of width 'dx'. The area added is approximately f(x) times dx. Therefore, the rate of change of Area (dA/dx) is exactly the height of the curve f(x).

section_5.title: The Fundamental Theorem: Two Sides of a Coin
section_5.content: Synthesize the observation: Differentiation and Integration are inverse operations. If you integrate a function to get the area, and then differentiate that area, you get the original function back.
section_5.example: A 'Mathematical Loop' animation: Start with f(x) -> Integrate -> Get Area Function F(x) -> Differentiate -> Return to f(x). Use the analogy of a 'climbing' robot (Integration) and its 'downhill' speed sensor (Differentiation).

section_6.title: Application: The Power of the Relationship
section_6.content: Explain why this matters: We can find areas without drawing thousands of tiny rectangles. We just need to find the 'Anti-derivative'.
section_6.example: Calculating the area under a parabola y=x². Instead of counting blocks, we find its anti-derivative (x³/3), plug in the endpoints, and get the exact area instantly. The Cheetah's total distance is simply the 'anti-derivative' of its speed function.

section_1.title: The Cheetah's Journey: Speed vs. Distance
lecture_lines: Meet our cheetah racing across the savanna.
Speedometer shows its instantaneous speed, the derivative.
Odometer tracks total distance covered, the integral.
animations: Fade in Cheetah [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/cheetah.svg] silhouette (#D4AF37) moving from left to right.

Display an Odometer (#FFFFFF) in top right; digits increase, label it "Distance (Integral)" (#FFD700).

section_2.title: Prerequisite Recap: Slope and Area
lecture_lines: Recall that derivatives represent the slope of curves.
In contrast, integrals represent the area under curves.
We will now link these two fundamental concepts.
animations: Draw a green curve (#00FF00); show a magenta tangent line (#FF00FF) sliding along it.
Shade the area under a segment of the green curve (#00FF00) in light green.
Display labels "Slope (Derivative)" and "Area (Integral)" in white (#FFFFFF) with arrows pointing to the visuals.

section_3.title: The Accumulation Function
lecture_lines: Imagine a moving curtain sweeping across a graph.
Shaded area grows as the curtain moves right.
This growing area defines the accumulation function.
As input x increases, the total area accumulates.
This function maps points to their total area.
animations: Draw a green curve f(t) (#00FF00) and a vertical white curtain line (#FFFFFF) at t=0.
Move the curtain to the right; fill the area behind it with light green.
Label the shaded region "A(x)" (#00FF00) and show it as a function of the curtain's position.
Start plotting an orange curve A(x) (#FF8C00) in a separate area, tracking the total shaded area.
Highlight the final orange curve A(x) (#FF8C00) as the representation of total accumulation.

section_4.title: The Core Insight: How Fast Does Area Grow?
lecture_lines: How fast does this accumulated area actually grow?
Consider a tiny sliver added at position x.
The sliver height is exactly the function's height.
Area added equals height times the tiny width.
The growth rate is the original function's height.
animations: Zoom into the right edge of the shaded area under f(x) (#00FF00).
Introduce a thin yellow rectangle (#FFFF00) of width "dx" at the boundary.
Label the height of the rectangle f(x) (#00FF00) and the width dx (#FFFFFF).
Show the formula "dA = f(x) * dx" in yellow (#FFFF00) next to the sliver.
Transform the formula to "dA/dx = f(x)" and highlight f(x) (#00FF00).

section_5.title: The Fundamental Theorem: Two Sides of a Coin
lecture_lines: The area's derivative is the original function's height.
Differentiation and integration are inverse operations.
Integrating a rate gives you the total accumulation.
Differentiating accumulation returns the original rate.
They are two sides of the same coin.
animations: Display f(x) (#00FF00) and its accumulation A(x) (#FF8C00) side-by-side.
Draw a cyan arrow labeled "Integrate" (#00FFFF) from f(x) to A(x).
Pulse the A(x) label (#FF8C00) while the "Integrate" arrow is active.
Draw a magenta arrow labeled "Differentiate" (#FF00FF) from A(x) back to f(x).
Show the text "Fundamental Theorem of Calculus" (#FFFFFF) centered between the functions.

section_6.title: Application: The Power of the Relationship
lecture_lines: This relationship lets us calculate areas with ease.
Find the anti-derivative to solve complex integrals.
Total distance is simply the anti-derivative of speed.
animations: Plot the curve y=x^2 (#00FF00) and shade the area from 0 to 2.
Display the anti-derivative F(x) = x^3/3 (#FFFFFF) and the evaluation F(2) - F(0).
Replace the area label with the result "8/3" (#FFFF00) and flash it.

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Data from storyboard
        title_text = "The Cheetah's Journey: Speed vs. Distance"
        lecture_lines = [
            "Meet our cheetah racing across the savanna.",
            "Speedometer shows its instantaneous speed, the derivative.",
            "Odometer tracks total distance covered, the integral."
        ]
        
        # Setup layout
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)
        
        # Colors
        CHEETAH_COLOR = "#D4AF37"
        SPEEDOMETER_COLOR = "#FFFFFF"
        ODOMETER_COLOR = "#FFFFFF"
        DERIVATIVE_COLOR = "#00FFFF"
        INTEGRAL_COLOR = "#FFD700"
        
        # ValueTrackers for synchronization
        time_tracker = ValueTracker(0)
        
        # Functions to drive animations
        # Speed function v(t) fluctuates around 1.5 units/s
        def get_speed():
            t = time_tracker.get_value()
            return 1.5 + 0.5 * np.sin(2 * t)
            
        # Distance function s(t) is the integral of v(t)
        # Scaled to fit the grid width (approx 5 units max)
        def get_distance():
            t = time_tracker.get_value()
            # Integral of 1.5 + 0.5*sin(2t) is 1.5t - 0.25*cos(2t) + C
            # Scale by 0.5 to keep it within the 6-unit grid
            return (1.5 * t - 0.25 * np.cos(2 * t) + 0.25) * 0.5

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Highlight current line
        self.lecture[0].set_color(CHEETAH_COLOR)
        
        # Cheetah silhouette placeholder
        cheetah = Triangle(color=CHEETAH_COLOR, fill_opacity=1).scale(0.2).rotate(-PI/2)
        cheetah.move_to(self.grid["B1"])
        
        # Movement updater
        cheetah.add_updater(lambda m: m.move_to(self.grid["B1"] + RIGHT * get_distance()))
        
        self.play(FadeIn(cheetah))
        self.play(time_tracker.animate.set_value(2), run_time=3, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(0.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Update lecture colors
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(DERIVATIVE_COLOR)
        
        # Speedometer: Circle with a needle
        speedometer_base = Circle(radius=0.4, color=SPEEDOMETER_COLOR)
        self.place_at_grid(speedometer_base, "D2")
        
        # Needle starts pointing up
        needle = Line(
            speedometer_base.get_center(), 
            speedometer_base.get_center() + UP * 0.35, 
            color=RED, 
            stroke_width=4
        )
        # Angle maps speed to a range (PI/2 +/- swing)
        needle.add_updater(lambda m: m.set_angle(PI/2 - (get_speed() - 1.5) * PI/2))
        
        speed_label = Text("Derivative of Distance", font_size=16, color=DERIVATIVE_COLOR)
        self.place_at_grid(speed_label, "D3")
        
        self.play(Create(speedometer_base), Create(needle), Write(speed_label))
        self.play(time_tracker.animate.set_value(4), run_time=3, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(0.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Update lecture colors
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(INTEGRAL_COLOR)
        
        # Odometer: Box with increasing digits
        odometer_box = Rectangle(width=1.2, height=0.4, color=ODOMETER_COLOR)
        self.place_at_grid(odometer_box, "F2")
        
        distance_val = DecimalNumber(0, num_decimal_places=2, color=WHITE, font_size=22)
        distance_val.add_updater(lambda m: m.set_value(get_distance()))
        distance_val.move_to(odometer_box.get_center())
        
        odo_label = Text("Integral of Speed", font_size=16, color=INTEGRAL_COLOR)
        self.place_at_grid(odo_label, "F3")
        
        self.play(Create(odometer_box), Write(distance_val), Write(odo_label))
        self.play(time_tracker.animate.set_value(6), run_time=3, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(1)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Data from storyboard
        title = "Prerequisite Recap: Slope and Area"
        lecture_lines = [
            "- Recall that derivatives represent the slope of curves.",
            "- In contrast, integrals represent the area under curves.",
            "- We will now link these two fundamental concepts."
        ]
        
        # Initialize layout
        self.setup_layout(title, lecture_lines)
        
        # Colors from storyboard/issues
        GREEN_CURVE = "#00FF00"
        MAGENTA_SLOPE = "#FF00FF"
        LIGHT_GREEN_AREA = "#90EE90"
        WHITE_COLOR = "#FFFFFF"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Highlight lecture line 1 in Magenta (matching tangent/slope visual)
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(MAGENTA_SLOPE))

        # Setup Axes in the right-side grid area (A1 to F6)
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[-3, 3, 1],
            y_range=[-2, 2, 1],
            x_length=5,
            y_length=4,
            axis_config={"include_tip": True, "color": WHITE_COLOR}
        ).set_z_index(0)
        self.place_in_area(axes, "A1", "F6")
        
        # Parabolic curve: y = 0.2x^2 - 1
        curve = axes.plot(lambda x: 0.2 * x**2 - 1, color=GREEN_CURVE)
        
        # ValueTracker for the tangent point x-coordinate
        t_val = ValueTracker(-2)
        
        # Dot at the tangent point
        dot = Dot(color=MAGENTA_SLOPE).set_z_index(2)
        dot.add_updater(lambda m: m.move_to(axes.c2p(t_val.get_value(), 0.2 * t_val.get_value()**2 - 1)))
        
        # Tangent line updated dynamically
        tangent_line = Line(color=MAGENTA_SLOPE).set_z_index(1)
        def update_tangent(m):
            x = t_val.get_value()
            y = 0.2 * x**2 - 1
            slope = 0.4 * x
            # Determine start and end points for a fixed length tangent
            p1 = axes.c2p(x - 0.8, y - slope * 0.8)
            p2 = axes.c2p(x + 0.8, y + slope * 0.8)
            m.put_start_and_end_on(p1, p2)
        tangent_line.add_updater(update_tangent)

        self.play(Create(axes), Create(curve))
        self.add(dot, tangent_line)
        # Animate the tangent sliding along the curve
        self.play(t_val.animate.set_value(0.5), run_time=3, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Highlight lecture line 2 in Light Green (matching area visual)
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(LIGHT_GREEN_AREA))
        
        # Create and animate the shaded area under the curve
        # Area from x = 0.5 to x = 2.5
        shaded_area = axes.get_area(curve, x_range=[0.5, 2.5], color=LIGHT_GREEN_AREA, opacity=0.4)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(shaded_area))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Transition to linking the concepts
        # Line 3 stays white
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE_COLOR))
        
        # Create labels
        label_slope = Text("Slope (Rate)", font_size=24, color=WHITE_COLOR)
        label_area = Text("Area (Accumulation)", font_size=24, color=WHITE_COLOR)
        
        # Position labels using grid
        self.place_at_grid(label_slope, "B2")  # Top left quadrant
        self.place_at_grid(label_area, "E5")   # Bottom right quadrant
        
        self.play(
            Write(label_slope),
            Write(label_area)
        )
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Imagine a moving curtain sweeping across a graph.",
            "Shaded area grows as the curtain moves right.",
            "This growing area defines the accumulation function.",
            "As input x increases, the total area accumulates.",
            "This function maps points to their total area."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Accumulation Function", lecture_lines)

        # Colors
        COLOR_F = "#00FF00"  # Green for f(t)
        COLOR_CURTAIN = "#FFFFFF"  # White for vertical line
        COLOR_A = "#FF8C00"  # Orange for A(x)

        # --- Setup Axes and Functions ---
        # Top Axes for f(t)
        top_axes = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 4.5, 1],
            y_range=[0, 2.5, 1],
            x_length=4.5,
            y_length=2.5,
            axis_config={"include_tip": True, "font_size": 18}
        )
        self.place_in_area(top_axes, "A1", "C6", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # f(t) = 0.3 sin(2t) + 1.2
        def f_func(t):
            return 0.3 * np.sin(2 * t) + 1.2
        
        f_graph = top_axes.plot(f_func, x_range=[0, 4], color=COLOR_F)
        f_label = MathTex("f(t)", color=COLOR_F, font_size=24)
        self.place_at_grid(f_label, "A1", scale_factor=0.8)

        # Bottom Axes for A(x)
        bottom_axes = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 4.5, 1],
            y_range=[0, 6, 2],
            x_length=4.5,
            y_length=2.5,
            axis_config={"include_tip": True, "font_size": 18}
        )
        self.place_in_area(bottom_axes, "D1", "F6", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # A(x) = Integral of f(t) from 0 to x
        # Integral of 0.3 sin(2t) + 1.2 is -0.15 cos(2t) + 1.2t + C
        # At x=0, A(0)=0 => -0.15 cos(0) + 0 + C = 0 => -0.15 + C = 0 => C = 0.15
        def A_func(x):
            return -0.15 * np.cos(2 * x) + 1.2 * x + 0.15

        a_graph_full = bottom_axes.plot(A_func, x_range=[0, 4], color=COLOR_A)
        a_label = MathTex("A(x) = \\int_0^x f(t) dt", color=COLOR_A, font_size=24)
        self.place_at_grid(a_label, "D1", scale_factor=0.8)

        # State Tracker
        x_tracker = ValueTracker(0)

        # Curtain Line
        curtain = Line(
            top_axes.c2p(0, 0), top_axes.c2p(0, 2),
            color=COLOR_CURTAIN, stroke_width=2
        )
        curtain.add_updater(lambda m: m.move_to(top_axes.c2p(x_tracker.get_value(), 1)))

        # Area Mobject (using Polygon for accumulation)
        area = VMobject(fill_color=COLOR_F, fill_opacity=0.4, stroke_width=0)
        def update_area(m):
            x_val = x_tracker.get_value()
            if x_val <= 0.01:
                m.set_points_as_corners([top_axes.c2p(0,0), top_axes.c2p(0,0)])
            else:
                points = [top_axes.c2p(0, 0)]
                t_vals = np.linspace(0, x_val, 30)
                points.extend([top_axes.c2p(t, f_func(t)) for t in t_vals])
                points.append(top_axes.c2p(x_val, 0))
                m.set_points_as_corners(points)
        area.add_updater(update_area)

        # Orange trace for A(x)
        a_trace = VMobject(color=COLOR_A, stroke_width=3)
        def update_trace(m):
            x_val = x_tracker.get_value()
            if x_val <= 0.01:
                m.set_points_as_corners([bottom_axes.c2p(0,0), bottom_axes.c2p(0,0)])
            else:
                t_vals = np.linspace(0, x_val, 30)
                m.set_points_as_corners([bottom_axes.c2p(t, A_func(t)) for t in t_vals])
        a_trace.add_updater(update_trace)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.play(
            Create(top_axes),
            Create(f_graph),
            Write(f_label),
            Create(curtain),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.add(area)
        self.play(
            x_tracker.animate.set_value(1.5),
            run_time=3,
            rate_func=linear
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.play(
            Create(bottom_axes),
            Write(a_label),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.add(a_trace)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.play(
            x_tracker.animate.set_value(3.5),
            run_time=4,
            rate_func=linear
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Dot on A(x) and connecting line logic
        dot = Dot(bottom_axes.c2p(3.5, A_func(3.5)), color=COLOR_A)
        v_line = DashedLine(
            top_axes.c2p(3.5, 0),
            bottom_axes.c2p(3.5, A_func(3.5)),
            color=WHITE,
            stroke_width=1
        )
        
        self.play(
            FadeIn(dot),
            Create(v_line),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.wait(2)

        # Clean up for last line
        self.lecture[4].set_color(WHITE)
        self.wait(1)

        )

        def f_func(x):
            return 0.15 * x**2 + 0.5
            
        curve = axes.plot(f_func, x_range=[0, 4.5], color=GREEN)
        # Accumulated area up to x = 3.0
        x_at = 3.0
        area = axes.get_area(curve, x_range=[0, x_at], color=GREEN, opacity=0.3)
        
        # Place graph elements on the grid
        graph_visual = VGroup(axes, curve, area)
        self.place_in_area(graph_visual, "C1", "F6", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(Create(axes), Create(curve), run_time=1.5)
        self.play(FadeIn(area), run_time=1)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Color the second line
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        dx = 0.25

        # Calculate width and height in screen units using c2p
        w = axes.c2p(dx, 0)[0] - axes.c2p(0, 0)[0]
        h = axes.c2p(0, f_func(x_at))[1] - axes.c2p(0, 0)[1]
        
        sliver = Rectangle(
            width=w,
            height=h,
            fill_color="#FFFF00",
            fill_opacity=0.6,
            stroke_width=1,
            stroke_color=WHITE
        )
        # Position sliver immediately following the area at x_at
        sliver.move_to(axes.c2p(x_at + dx/2, f_func(x_at)/2))
        
        x_label = MathTex("x", font_size=24, color=WHITE).next_to(axes.c2p(x_at, 0), DOWN, buff=0.1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===

        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2

        # Draw a clockwise arrow labeled "Integrate" (#00FFFF).
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        integrate_arrow = CurvedArrow(

            color="#00FFFF"

        integrate_text = Text("Integrate", font_size=18, color="#00FFFF")

        # The arrow leads to F(x) (#FF8C00) at the bottom.

        Fx_label = MathTex("F(x)", color="#FF8C00")

        self.play(Write(Fx_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # L4: "Differentiating accumulation returns the original rate."

        diff_arrow = CurvedArrow(

        # Display the text "Fundamental Theorem of Calculus" (#FFFFFF) in the center.

        ftc_text = Text("Fundamental Theorem\nof Calculus", font_size=20, color=WHITE, line_spacing=0.8)
        self.place_in_area(ftc_text, 'C3', 'D4')
        
        loop_group = VGroup(fx_label, integrate_arrow, Fx_label, diff_arrow, integrate_text, diff_text)
        self.play(Flash(loop_group, color=WHITE, line_length=0.4, flash_radius=1.5))
        self.play(Write(ftc_text))
        self.wait(2)

            "Speedometer shows its instantaneous speed, the derivative.",
            "Odometer tracks total distance covered, the integral."
        ]
        
        # Setup layout
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)
        
        # Colors
        CHEETAH_COLOR = "#D4AF37"
        SPEEDOMETER_COLOR = "#FFFFFF"
        ODOMETER_COLOR = "#FFFFFF"
        DERIVATIVE_COLOR = "#00FFFF"
        INTEGRAL_COLOR = "#FFD700"
        
        # ValueTrackers for synchronization
        time_tracker = ValueTracker(0)
        
        # Functions to drive animations
        # Speed function v(t) fluctuates around 1.5 units/s
        def get_speed():
            t = time_tracker.get_value()
            return 1.5 + 0.5 * np.sin(2 * t)
            
        # Distance function s(t) is the integral of v(t)
        # Scaled to fit the grid width (approx 5 units max)
        def get_distance():
            t = time_tracker.get_value()
            # Integral of 1.5 + 0.5*sin(2t) is 1.5t - 0.25*cos(2t) + C
            # Scale by 0.5 to keep it within the 6-unit grid
            return (1.5 * t - 0.25 * np.cos(2 * t) + 0.25) * 0.5

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Highlight current line
        self.lecture[0].set_color(CHEETAH_COLOR)
        
        # Cheetah silhouette placeholder
        cheetah = Triangle(color=CHEETAH_COLOR, fill_opacity=1).scale(0.2).rotate(-PI/2)
        cheetah.move_to(self.grid["B1"])
        
        # Movement updater
        cheetah.add_updater(lambda m: m.move_to(self.grid["B1"] + RIGHT * get_distance()))
        
        self.play(FadeIn(cheetah))
        self.play(time_tracker.animate.set_value(2), run_time=3, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(0.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Update lecture colors
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(DERIVATIVE_COLOR)
        
        # Speedometer: Circle with a needle
        speedometer_base = Circle(radius=0.4, color=SPEEDOMETER_COLOR)
        self.place_at_grid(speedometer_base, "D2")
        
        # Needle starts pointing up
        needle = Line(
            speedometer_base.get_center(), 
            speedometer_base.get_center() + UP * 0.35, 
            color=RED, 
            stroke_width=4
        )
        # Angle maps speed to a range (PI/2 +/- swing)
        needle.add_updater(lambda m: m.set_angle(PI/2 - (get_speed() - 1.5) * PI/2))
        
        speed_label = Text("Derivative of Distance", font_size=16, color=DERIVATIVE_COLOR)
        self.place_at_grid(speed_label, "D3")
        
        self.play(Create(speedometer_base), Create(needle), Write(speed_label))
        self.play(time_tracker.animate.set_value(4), run_time=3, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(0.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Update lecture colors
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(INTEGRAL_COLOR)
        
        # Odometer: Box with increasing digits
        odometer_box = Rectangle(width=1.2, height=0.4, color=ODOMETER_COLOR)
        self.place_at_grid(odometer_box, "F2")
        
        distance_val = DecimalNumber(0, num_decimal_places=2, color=WHITE, font_size=22)
        distance_val.add_updater(lambda m: m.set_value(get_distance()))
        distance_val.move_to(odometer_box.get_center())
        
        odo_label = Text("Integral of Speed", font_size=16, color=INTEGRAL_COLOR)
        self.place_at_grid(odo_label, "F3")
        
        self.play(Create(odometer_box), Write(distance_val), Write(odo_label))
        self.play(time_tracker.animate.set_value(6), run_time=3, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(1)

outline.title: The Fundamental Theorem: Two Sides of a Coin
outline.content: Synthesize the observation: Differentiation and Integration are inverse operations. If you integrate a function to get the area, and then differentiate that area, you get the original function back.
outline.example: A 'Mathematical Loop' animation: Start with f(x) -> Integrate -> Get Area Function F(x) -> Differentiate -> Return to f(x). Use the analogy of a 'climbing' robot (Integration) and its 'downhill' speed sensor (Differentiation).

storyboard.title: The Fundamental Theorem: Two Sides of a Coin
lecture_lines: The area's derivative is the original function's height.
Differentiation and integration are inverse operations.
Integrating a rate gives you the total accumulation.
Differentiating accumulation returns the original rate.
They are two sides of the same coin.
animations: Display f(x) (#00FF00) and its accumulation A(x) (#FF8C00) side-by-side.
Draw a cyan arrow labeled "Integrate" (#00FFFF) from f(x) to A(x).
Pulse the A(x) label (#FF8C00) while the "Integrate" arrow is active.
Draw a magenta arrow labeled "Differentiate" (#FF00FF) from A(x) back to f(x).
Show the text "Fundamental Theorem of Calculus" (#FFFFFF) centered between the functions.

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Fundamental Theorem: Two Sides of a Coin", [
            "The area's derivative is the original function's height.",
            "Differentiation and integration are inverse operations.",
            "Integrating a rate gives you the total accumulation.",
            "Differentiating accumulation returns the original rate.",
            "They are two sides of the same coin."
        ])

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # L1: "The area's derivative is the original function's height."
        # Place f(x) (#00FF00) at the top.
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#00FF00"))
        fx_label = MathTex("f(x)", color="#00FF00")
        self.place_in_area(fx_label, 'B3', 'B4', scale_factor=1.2)
        self.play(Write(fx_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # L2: "Differentiation and integration are inverse operations."
        # Draw a clockwise arrow labeled "Integrate" (#00FFFF).
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        integrate_arrow = CurvedArrow(
            start_point=self.grid['B5'] + RIGHT*0.2, 
            end_point=self.grid['E5'] + RIGHT*0.2, 
            angle=-PI/1.2, 
            color="#00FFFF"
        )
        integrate_text = Text("Integrate", font_size=18, color="#00FFFF")
        self.place_at_grid(integrate_text, 'C6')
        self.play(Create(integrate_arrow), Write(integrate_text))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # L3: "Integrating a rate gives you the total accumulation."
        # The arrow leads to F(x) (#FF8C00) at the bottom.
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FF8C00"))
        Fx_label = MathTex("F(x)", color="#FF8C00")
        self.place_in_area(Fx_label, 'E3', 'E4', scale_factor=1.2)
        self.play(Write(Fx_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # L4: "Differentiating accumulation returns the original rate."
        # Draw another clockwise arrow labeled "Differentiate" (#FF00FF) from F(x) back to f(x).
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color("#FF00FF"))
        diff_arrow = CurvedArrow(
            start_point=self.grid['E2'] + LEFT*0.2, 
            end_point=self.grid['B2'] + LEFT*0.2, 
            angle=-PI/1.2, 
            color="#FF00FF"
        )
        diff_text = Text("Differentiate", font_size=18, color="#FF00FF")
        self.place_at_grid(diff_text, 'D1')
        self.play(Create(diff_arrow), Write(diff_text))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # L5: "They are two sides of the same coin."
        # Flash the entire loop in white (#FFFFFF) to emphasize the cycle.
        # Display the text "Fundamental Theorem of Calculus" (#FFFFFF) in the center.
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        ftc_text = Text("Fundamental Theorem\nof Calculus", font_size=20, color=WHITE, line_spacing=0.8)
        self.place_in_area(ftc_text, 'C3', 'D4')
        
        loop_group = VGroup(fx_label, integrate_arrow, Fx_label, diff_arrow, integrate_text, diff_text)
        self.play(Flash(loop_group, color=WHITE, line_length=0.4, flash_radius=1.5))
        self.play(Write(ftc_text))
        self.wait(2)

outline.title: Prerequisite Recap: Slope and Area

from manim import *
import numpy as np

# Use the provided TeachingScene base class without modification.
class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Data from storyboard
        title = "Prerequisite Recap: Slope and Area"
        lecture_lines = [
            "- Recall that derivatives represent the slope of curves.",
            "- In contrast, integrals represent the area under curves.",
            "- We will now link these two fundamental concepts."
        ]
        
        # Initialize layout
        self.setup_layout(title, lecture_lines)
        
        # Colors from storyboard/issues
        GREEN_CURVE = "#00FF00"
        MAGENTA_SLOPE = "#FF00FF"
        LIGHT_GREEN_AREA = "#90EE90"
        WHITE_COLOR = "#FFFFFF"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Highlight lecture line 1 in Magenta (matching tangent/slope visual)
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(MAGENTA_SLOPE))

        # Setup Axes in the right-side grid area (A1 to F6)
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[-3, 3, 1],
            y_range=[-2, 2, 1],
            x_length=5,
            y_length=4,
            axis_config={"include_tip": True, "color": WHITE_COLOR}
        ).set_z_index(0)
        self.place_in_area(axes, "A1", "F6")
        
        # Parabolic curve: y = 0.2x^2 - 1
        curve = axes.plot(lambda x: 0.2 * x**2 - 1, color=GREEN_CURVE)
        
        # ValueTracker for the tangent point x-coordinate
        t_val = ValueTracker(-2)
        
        # Dot at the tangent point
        dot = Dot(color=MAGENTA_SLOPE).set_z_index(2)
        dot.add_updater(lambda m: m.move_to(axes.c2p(t_val.get_value(), 0.2 * t_val.get_value()**2 - 1)))
        
        # Tangent line updated dynamically
        tangent_line = Line(color=MAGENTA_SLOPE).set_z_index(1)
        def update_tangent(m):
            x = t_val.get_value()
            y = 0.2 * x**2 - 1
            slope = 0.4 * x
            # Determine start and end points for a fixed length tangent
            p1 = axes.c2p(x - 0.8, y - slope * 0.8)
            p2 = axes.c2p(x + 0.8, y + slope * 0.8)
            m.put_start_and_end_on(p1, p2)
        tangent_line.add_updater(update_tangent)

        self.wait(1)

        # Transition to linking the concepts
        # Line 3 stays white
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE_COLOR))
        
        # Create labels
        label_slope = Text("Slope (Rate)", font_size=24, color=WHITE_COLOR)
        label_area = Text("Area (Accumulation)", font_size=24, color=WHITE_COLOR)
        
        # Position labels using grid

        self.place_at_grid(label_area, "E5")   # Bottom right quadrant

            Write(label_slope),
            Write(label_area)
        )

import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Imagine a moving curtain sweeping across a graph.",
            "Shaded area grows as the curtain moves right.",
            "This growing area defines the accumulation function.",
            "As input x increases, the total area accumulates.",
            "This function maps points to their total area."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Accumulation Function", lecture_lines)

        # Colors
        COLOR_F = "#00FF00"  # Green for f(t)
        COLOR_CURTAIN = "#FFFFFF"  # White for vertical line
        COLOR_A = "#FF8C00"  # Orange for A(x)

        # --- Setup Axes and Functions ---
        # Top Axes for f(t)
        top_axes = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 4.5, 1],
            y_range=[0, 2.5, 1],
            x_length=4.5,
            y_length=2.5,
            axis_config={"include_tip": True, "font_size": 18}
        )
        self.place_in_area(top_axes, "A1", "C6", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # f(t) = 0.3 sin(2t) + 1.2
        def f_func(t):
            return 0.3 * np.sin(2 * t) + 1.2
        
        f_graph = top_axes.plot(f_func, x_range=[0, 4], color=COLOR_F)
        f_label = MathTex("f(t)", color=COLOR_F, font_size=24)
        self.place_at_grid(f_label, "A1", scale_factor=0.8)

        # Bottom Axes for A(x)
        bottom_axes = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 4.5, 1],
            y_range=[0, 6, 2],
            x_length=4.5,
            y_length=2.5,
            axis_config={"include_tip": True, "font_size": 18}
        )
        self.place_in_area(bottom_axes, "D1", "F6", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # A(x) = Integral of f(t) from 0 to x
        # Integral of 0.3 sin(2t) + 1.2 is -0.15 cos(2t) + 1.2t + C
        # At x=0, A(0)=0 => -0.15 cos(0) + 0 + C = 0 => -0.15 + C = 0 => C = 0.15
        def A_func(x):
            return -0.15 * np.cos(2 * x) + 1.2 * x + 0.15

        a_graph_full = bottom_axes.plot(A_func, x_range=[0, 4], color=COLOR_A)
        a_label = MathTex("A(x) = \\int_0^x f(t) dt", color=COLOR_A, font_size=24)
        self.place_at_grid(a_label, "D1", scale_factor=0.8)

        # State Tracker
        x_tracker = ValueTracker(0)

        # Curtain Line
        curtain = Line(
            top_axes.c2p(0, 0), top_axes.c2p(0, 2),
            color=COLOR_CURTAIN, stroke_width=2
        )
        curtain.add_updater(lambda m: m.move_to(top_axes.c2p(x_tracker.get_value(), 1)))

        # Area Mobject (using Polygon for accumulation)
        area = VMobject(fill_color=COLOR_F, fill_opacity=0.4, stroke_width=0)
        def update_area(m):
            x_val = x_tracker.get_value()
            if x_val <= 0.01:
                m.set_points_as_corners([top_axes.c2p(0,0), top_axes.c2p(0,0)])
            else:
                points = [top_axes.c2p(0, 0)]
                t_vals = np.linspace(0, x_val, 30)
                points.extend([top_axes.c2p(t, f_func(t)) for t in t_vals])
                points.append(top_axes.c2p(x_val, 0))
                m.set_points_as_corners(points)
        area.add_updater(update_area)

        # Orange trace for A(x)
        a_trace = VMobject(color=COLOR_A, stroke_width=3)
        def update_trace(m):
            x_val = x_tracker.get_value()
            if x_val <= 0.01:
                m.set_points_as_corners([bottom_axes.c2p(0,0), bottom_axes.c2p(0,0)])
            else:
                t_vals = np.linspace(0, x_val, 30)
                m.set_points_as_corners([bottom_axes.c2p(t, A_func(t)) for t in t_vals])
        a_trace.add_updater(update_trace)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.play(
            Create(top_axes),
            Create(f_graph),
            Write(f_label),
            Create(curtain),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.add(area)
        self.play(
            x_tracker.animate.set_value(1.5),
            run_time=3,
            rate_func=linear
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.play(
            Create(bottom_axes),
            Write(a_label),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.add(a_trace)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.play(
            x_tracker.animate.set_value(3.5),
            run_time=4,
            rate_func=linear
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Dot on A(x) and connecting line logic
        dot = Dot(bottom_axes.c2p(3.5, A_func(3.5)), color=COLOR_A)
        v_line = DashedLine(
            top_axes.c2p(3.5, 0),
            bottom_axes.c2p(3.5, A_func(3.5)),
            color=WHITE,
            stroke_width=1
        )
        
        self.play(
            FadeIn(dot),

            run_time=1.5
        )

        # Clean up for last line

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup data from storyboard
        title = "The Core Insight: How Fast Does Area Grow?"
        lines = [
            "How fast does this accumulated area actually grow?",
            "Consider a tiny sliver added at position x.",
            "The sliver height is exactly the function's height.",
            "Area added equals height times the tiny width.",
            "The growth rate is the original function's height."
        ]
        
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Color the first line
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Setup the plot
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 5, 1],
            y_range=[0, 4, 1],
            x_length=5,
            y_length=4,
            axis_config={"include_tip": True, "color": GREY}
        )
        
        # Define the function f(x)
        def f_func(x):
            return 0.15 * x**2 + 0.5
            
        curve = axes.plot(f_func, x_range=[0, 4.5], color="#00FF00")
        # Accumulated area up to x = 3.0
        x_at = 3.0
        area = axes.get_area(curve, x_range=[0, x_at], color="#00FF00", opacity=0.3)
        
        # Place graph elements on the grid
        # Fix for Issue 35: Move graph_visual to D1-F6 with scale 0.9
        graph_visual = VGroup(axes, curve, area)
        self.place_in_area(graph_visual, "D1", "F6", scale_factor=0.9)
        
        self.play(Create(axes), Create(curve), run_time=1.5)
        self.play(FadeIn(area), run_time=1)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Color the second line
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        dx = 0.25
        # Rectangle representing the 'extra sliver'
        w = axes.c2p(dx, 0)[0] - axes.c2p(0, 0)[0]
        h = axes.c2p(0, f_func(x_at))[1] - axes.c2p(0, 0)[1]
        
        sliver = Rectangle(
            width=w,
            height=h,
            fill_color="#FFFF00",
            fill_opacity=0.6,
            stroke_width=1,
            stroke_color=WHITE
        )
        # Position sliver immediately following the area at x_at
        sliver.move_to(axes.c2p(x_at + dx/2, f_func(x_at)/2))
        
        x_label = MathTex("x", font_size=24, color=WHITE).next_to(axes.c2p(x_at, 0), DOWN, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(Create(sliver), Write(x_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Color the third line
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#00FF00")
        
        # Brace for vertical dimension
        h_brace = Brace(sliver, LEFT, buff=0.05)
        h_label = MathTex("f(x)", color="#00FF00", font_size=24).next_to(h_brace, LEFT, buff=0.05)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(h_brace), Write(h_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Color the fourth line
        self.lecture[3].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Brace for horizontal dimension
        w_brace = Brace(sliver, DOWN, buff=0.05)
        w_label = MathTex("dx", color="#FFFFFF", font_size=24).next_to(w_brace, DOWN, buff=0.05)
        
        # Display Area Formula
        # Fix for Issue 36: Move formula_1 to B2-B5
        formula_1 = MathTex("dA = f(x) \\cdot dx", color="#FFFF00", font_size=32)
        self.place_in_area(formula_1, "B2", "B5", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(w_brace), Write(w_label))
        self.play(Write(formula_1))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # Color the fifth line
        self.lecture[4].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Transform to Derivative Formula
        # Fix for Issue 36: Move formula_2 to B2-B5
        # Highlight f(x) with Green color
        formula_2 = MathTex(r"\frac{dA}{dx} =", "f(x)", color="#FFFF00", font_size=32)
        formula_2.set_color_by_tex("f(x)", "#00FF00")
        self.place_in_area(formula_2, "B2", "B5", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(Transform(formula_1, formula_2))
        
        # Visual Emphasis
        h_rect = SurroundingRectangle(formula_1, color=YELLOW, buff=0.1)
        self.play(Create(h_rect))
        
        # Summary label
        # Fix for Issue 37: Move summary to C2-C5 with scale 0.8
        summary = Text("Slope of A(x) is f(x)", font_size=22, color=YELLOW)
        self.place_in_area(summary, "C2", "C5", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(FadeIn(summary))
        
        self.wait(2)

            return (1.5 * t - 0.25 * np.cos(2 * t) + 0.25) * 0.5

    def construct(self):
        # Data from storyboard
        title = "Prerequisite Recap: Slope and Area"
        lecture_lines = [
            "- Recall that derivatives represent the slope of curves.",
            "- In contrast, integrals represent the area under curves.",
            "- We will now link these two fundamental concepts."
        ]
        
        # Initialize layout
        self.setup_layout(title, lecture_lines)
        
        # Colors from storyboard
        GREEN_CURVE = "#00FF00"
        MAGENTA_SLOPE = "#FF00FF"
        LIGHT_GREEN_AREA = "#90EE90"
        WHITE_COLOR = "#FFFFFF"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Highlight lecture line 1 in Magenta (matching tangent/slope visual)
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(MAGENTA_SLOPE))

        # Setup Axes in the right-side grid area (A1 to F6)
        # Issue 31: scale_factor=0.85
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[-3, 3, 1],
            y_range=[-2, 2, 1],
            x_length=5,
            y_length=4,
            axis_config={"include_tip": True, "color": WHITE_COLOR}
        ).set_z_index(0)
        self.place_in_area(axes, "A1", "F6", scale_factor=0.85)
        
        # Parabolic curve: y = 0.2x^2 - 1
        curve = axes.plot(lambda x: 0.2 * x**2 - 1, color=GREEN_CURVE)
        
        # ValueTracker for the tangent point x-coordinate
        t_val = ValueTracker(-2)
        
        # Dot at the tangent point
        dot = Dot(color=MAGENTA_SLOPE).set_z_index(2)
        dot.add_updater(lambda m: m.move_to(axes.c2p(t_val.get_value(), 0.2 * t_val.get_value()**2 - 1)))
        
        # Tangent line updated dynamically
        tangent_line = Line(color=MAGENTA_SLOPE).set_z_index(1)
        def update_tangent(m):
            x = t_val.get_value()
            y = 0.2 * x**2 - 1
            slope = 0.4 * x
            # Determine start and end points for a fixed length tangent
            p1 = axes.c2p(x - 0.8, y - slope * 0.8)
            p2 = axes.c2p(x + 0.8, y + slope * 0.8)
            m.put_start_and_end_on(p1, p2)
        tangent_line.add_updater(update_tangent)

        self.play(Create(axes), Create(curve))
        self.add(dot, tangent_line)
        # Animate the tangent sliding along the curve
        self.play(t_val.animate.set_value(0.5), run_time=3, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Highlight lecture line 2 in Light Green (matching area visual)
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(LIGHT_GREEN_AREA))
        
        # Create and animate the shaded area under the curve
        # Area from x = 0.5 to x = 2.5
        shaded_area = axes.get_area(curve, x_range=[0.5, 2.5], color=LIGHT_GREEN_AREA, opacity=0.4)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(shaded_area))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Transition to linking the concepts
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE_COLOR))
        
        # Create labels as per storyboard: "Slope (Derivative)" and "Area (Integral)"
        label_slope = Text("Slope (Derivative)", font_size=24, color=WHITE_COLOR)
        label_area = Text("Area (Integral)", font_size=24, color=WHITE_COLOR)
        
        # Position labels using grid
        # Issue 29: place_at_grid(label_slope, 'A2', scale_factor=0.7)
        # Issue 30: place_at_grid(label_area, 'F5', scale_factor=0.7)
        self.place_at_grid(label_slope, "A2", scale_factor=0.7)
        self.place_at_grid(label_area, "F5", scale_factor=0.7)
        
        # Create arrows pointing to the visuals
        arrow_slope = Arrow(
            start=label_slope.get_bottom(),
            end=dot.get_center(),
            buff=0.1,
            color=WHITE_COLOR,
            stroke_width=2,
            max_tip_length_to_length_ratio=0.2
        )
        
        # Point to the center of the shaded area
        area_center = axes.c2p(1.5, -0.5) # Approximate center of shaded region
        arrow_area = Arrow(
            start=label_area.get_top(),
            end=area_center,
            buff=0.1,
            color=WHITE_COLOR,
            stroke_width=2,
            max_tip_length_to_length_ratio=0.2
        )

        self.play(
            Write(label_slope),
            Write(label_area),
            Create(arrow_slope),
            Create(arrow_area)
        )
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Imagine a moving curtain sweeping across a graph.",
            "Shaded area grows as the curtain moves right.",
            "This growing area defines the accumulation function.",
            "As input x increases, the total area accumulates.",
            "This function maps points to their total area."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Accumulation Function", lecture_lines)

        # Colors
        COLOR_F = "#00FF00"  # Green for f(t)
        COLOR_CURTAIN = "#FFFFFF"  # White for vertical line
        COLOR_A = "#FF8C00"  # Orange for A(x)

        # --- Setup Axes and Functions ---
        # Top Axes for f(t)
        top_axes = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 4.5, 1],
            y_range=[0, 2.5, 1],
            x_length=4.0,
            y_length=2.0,
            axis_config={"include_tip": True, "font_size": 18}
        )

        def f_func(t):
            return 0.3 * np.sin(2 * t) + 1.2

        bottom_axes = Axes(

            y_length=2.0,

        )
        # Issue 33 fix: start from D2 instead of D1 to maintain margin
        self.place_in_area(bottom_axes, "D2", "F6", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # A(x) = Integral of f(t) from 0 to x
        # Integral of 0.3 sin(2t) + 1.2 is -0.15 cos(2t) + 1.2t + C
        # At x=0, A(0)=0 => -0.15 cos(0) + 0 + C = 0 => -0.15 + C = 0 => C = 0.15
        def A_func(x):
            return -0.15 * np.cos(2 * x) + 1.2 * x + 0.15

        # Issue 34 fix: scale factor 0.7 at D1 to avoid crowding lecture notes

        # State Tracker
        x_tracker = ValueTracker(0)

        # Curtain Line

            top_axes.c2p(0, 0), top_axes.c2p(0, 2.2),
            color=COLOR_CURTAIN, stroke_width=2
        )
        curtain.add_updater(lambda m: m.move_to(top_axes.c2p(x_tracker.get_value(), 1.1)))

        # Area Mobject (using Polygon for accumulation)
        area = VMobject(fill_color=COLOR_F, fill_opacity=0.4, stroke_width=0)
        def update_area(m):
            x_val = x_tracker.get_value()
            if x_val <= 0.01:
                m.set_points_as_corners([top_axes.c2p(0,0), top_axes.c2p(0.01, 0)])
            else:
                points = [top_axes.c2p(0, 0)]
                t_vals = np.linspace(0, x_val, 30)
                points.extend([top_axes.c2p(t, f_func(t)) for t in t_vals])
                points.append(top_axes.c2p(x_val, 0))
                m.set_points_as_corners(points)
        area.add_updater(update_area)

        # Orange trace for A(x)
        a_trace = VMobject(color=COLOR_A, stroke_width=3)
        def update_trace(m):
            x_val = x_tracker.get_value()
            if x_val <= 0.01:
                m.set_points_as_corners([bottom_axes.c2p(0,0), bottom_axes.c2p(0.01,0)])
            else:

                m.set_points_as_corners([bottom_axes.c2p(t, A_func(t)) for t in t_vals])
        a_trace.add_updater(update_trace)

        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.play(
            Create(top_axes),
            Create(f_graph),
            Write(f_label),
            Create(curtain),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Shaded area grows as the curtain moves right.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.add(area)
        self.play(
            x_tracker.animate.set_value(1.5),
            run_time=3,
            rate_func=linear
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # This growing area defines the accumulation function.
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.play(
            Create(bottom_axes),
            Write(a_label),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.add(a_trace)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # As input x increases, the total area accumulates.
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.play(
            x_tracker.animate.set_value(3.5),
            run_time=4,
            rate_func=linear
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # This function maps points to their total area.
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Dot on A(x) and connecting line logic
        dot = Dot(bottom_axes.c2p(3.5, A_func(3.5)), color=COLOR_A)
        v_line = DashedLine(
            top_axes.c2p(3.5, 0),
            bottom_axes.c2p(3.5, A_func(3.5)),
            color=WHITE,
            stroke_width=1
        )
        
        self.play(
            FadeIn(dot),
            Create(v_line),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.wait(2)
